narrative: A [[sketcher]] opens [[app|excalidraw.com]], which is a thin wrapper around the [[editor]].
Every click and drag becomes an [[actions|editing action]] on shapes from the [[geometry]] packages.
[[render|Rendering]] paints the scene on canvas, and [[files]] saves it or exports it as an image.
To draw together, the app encrypts every change and sends it to the others live over [[svc-socketio]], and keeps shared scenes in [[store-firestore|Firestore]], with images in [[svc-cloud-storage]].
A [[developer]] can embed the same editor in their own app, like the [[extras|examples]] do.

tours.title: From excalidraw.com to pixels
captions: The site's app component renders the Excalidraw editor from the package's public entry point.
The package entry wraps the main editor component with its providers.
The editor component renders its canvases, stacked on top of each other.
The canvas layer picks the static canvas for the finished shapes.
The static canvas asks the renderer to paint every visible shape, with Rough.js for the hand-drawn look.

tours.title: Exporting a PNG
captions: The menu layer opens the image export dialog.
The dialog previews the image; when you press save it hands the scene to the data module's export helper.
The helper asks the scene exporter for a canvas or SVG of the scene, then saves it as a file or copies it.
Export draws the scene off-screen with the chosen background, padding and scale, reusing the same static renderer the editor paints with, so the image matches the screen.

tours.title: Changing a shape's style
captions: With a shape selected, the menu layer shows the shape properties panel.
The panel doesn't draw its own controls: it asks each registered action to render its panel.
The properties action renders the stroke and background controls and applies a change to every selected shape.

tours.title: Saving a shared scene
captions: The site's app starts the collaboration component when you start a live session or open a shared link.
Collaboration encrypts the scene in the browser and saves it as people draw, so newcomers can load it.
The Firebase module writes the encrypted scene to Firestore; the key never leaves the link.

tours.title: Drawing together live
captions: The share dialog's start-session button asks the collaboration component to open a live room.
Collaboration connects to the room server over Socket.IO, encrypts every change in the browser and broadcasts it, so everyone in the room sees each stroke as it happens.
